event: Seti River flood (Annapurna IV rock-ice avalanche)
seismic_evidence: ISC catalogue MS 3.9 at 03:25:01 UTC; surface waves at IC.LSA Lhasa (702 km) 242 s later, ~130x background (0.02-0.08 Hz); also flagged by Lamont/GSN

summary: A rain-triggered landslide at Jure buried a village and dammed the Sunkoshi; the 2:36 am failure registered as a local ML 3.3 seismic event.

seismic_evidence: Triggered by the Mw 7.8 Gorkha earthquake (06:11 UTC); avalanche signal masked by the quake
summary: The Mw 7.8 Gorkha earthquake triggered a rock-ice avalanche and air blast that erased Langtang village; more than 350 people died or went missing.

seismic_evidence: Moraine collapse timed seismically at 22:13:20 IST (Sattar et al. 2025 Science); open IO.EVN record (136 km) gappy/unusable
summary: A frozen-moraine collapse into South Lhonak lake triggered a GLOF down the Teesta; seismic data timed the onset to 22:13:20 IST.

seismic_evidence: IO.EVN (23 km): data gap at the event, elevated 1-8 Hz tremor (~4x) for ~35 min after; seismic data used in NHESS 2026 study
summary: A wet-snow avalanche into the Thyanbo lakes triggered a cascading outburst that buried part of Thame village in the Khumbu; daytime timing let people escape.

seismic_evidence: NK.KKN (54 km) shows an emergent 3-20 Hz rumble building over ~2 h; K. Cook reported the flood visible seismically ~1 h before it reached the border; not catalogued
source: Wikipedia 2025 Nepal floods; Petley EOS Landslide Blog
summary: A supraglacial lake in Kyirong County (Tibet) drained into the Lende Khola, sweeping away the Friendship Bridge and Rasuwagadhi dry port and damaging three hydropower plants — the same corridor, 13 months before 2026.

seismic_evidence: USGS us7000tbwb Ms 5.2 'landslide'; EMSC Ms 5.2; ISC/IDC Mw 5.7 (CTBTO). NK.KKN (57 km) 110x at collapse, flood rumble peaks 41 min later (~28x); IO.EVN 113x; AM.R3B1E Melamchi 45x
summary: A rock-ice avalanche from the north flank of Tsangbu Ri (Langtang Lirung massif) turned into a debris flow and flood that ran down the Lende Khola, Bhotekoshi and Trishuli. Gyirong Port was hit ~7 minutes after the collapse; 12 hydropower projects were damaged.
